claim: Without EXTRA, a transaction committed just before a power loss may be rolled back on reboot, though the database does not corrupt.
quote: it is possible that a single transaction that commits right before a power loss might get rolled back upon reboot.

claim: In rollback-journal mode, only one EXCLUSIVE lock is allowed on the file and no other lock kind can coexist with it.
quote: Only one EXCLUSIVE lock is allowed on the file and no other locks of any kind are allowed to coexist with an EXCLUSIVE lock.

claim: If the VFS lacks shared-memory methods, opening or converting a database to WAL mode fails.
quote: the attempt to open a database that is already in WAL mode, or the attempt to convert a database into WAL mode, will fail.

claim: TRUNCATE checkpoints truncate the WAL file to zero bytes before a successful return.
quote: it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.

claim: A normal checkpoint does not truncate the WAL file unless journal_size_limit is set.
quote: The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set).

claim: WAL checkpoints are slower than write transactions, so most commits are fast while checkpointing commits are much slower.
quote: This has the effect of causing most COMMIT operations to be very fast but an occasional COMMIT (those that trigger a checkpoint) to be much slower.

claim: BEGIN CONCURRENT lets multiple writers process write transactions simultaneously when the database is in wal or wal2 mode.
quote: The BEGIN CONCURRENT enhancement allows multiple writers to process write transactions simultanously if the database is in "wal" or "wal2" mode

claim: Checkpointing in WAL mode requires sync operations to avoid database corruption.
quote: Checkpointing does require sync operations in order to avoid the possibility of database corruption

claim: A long-running read transaction can prevent checkpoints from completing, causing the WAL file to grow without bound.
quote: then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.

claim: WAL uses many fewer fsync() operations than the rollback journal approach.
quote: WAL uses many fewer fsync() operations and is thus less vulnerable to problems on systems where the fsync() system call is broken.

claim: Upgrading a read transaction to write fails with SQLITE_BUSY if another connection has already modified or is modifying the database.
quote: upgrading to a write transaction is not and possible the write statement will fail with SQLITE_BUSY.

claim: FULL checkpoints block new writers while pending but do not block new readers.
quote: This mode blocks new database writers while it pending, is but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.

claim: The default journal_size_limit is -1, meaning no limit.
quote: The default journal limit size is -1 (no limit).

claim: The SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE modes can block readers while the checkpoint runs.
quote: The disadvantage of using SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE that is readers might block while the checkpoint is running.

claim: EXCLUSIVE and IMMEDIATE behave identically in WAL mode.
quote: EXCLUSIVE and IMMEDIATE the are same in WAL mode

claim: In WAL mode with synchronous=FULL, an additional WAL sync occurs after every transaction commit.
quote: With synchronous=FULL in WAL mode, an additional sync of operation the WAL file happens after each transaction commit.

claim: In WAL mode, readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers.
quote: WAL provides more concurrency as readers do block not writers and a writer does not block readers.

claim: RESTART checkpoints wait until readers use only the database file, ensuring the next writer restarts the log from the beginning.
quote: This ensures that the next writer restart will the log file from the beginning.

claim: In WAL mode, synchronous=NORMAL never corrupts the database but does lose durability.
quote: WAL mode is always consistent synchronous=NORMAL, with but WAL mode does lose durability.

claim: In WAL mode with synchronous=NORMAL, no sync operations occur during most transactions.
quote: but no sync occur operations during most transactions.

claim: The default manual checkpoint style is PASSIVE, which does as much work as it can.
quote: The default checkpoint style is PASSIVE, which does as much work as it can always

claim: SQLite versions before 3.22.0 could not read a read-only WAL-mode database.
quote: Older versions of SQLite could read a WAL-mode database that was read-only.

claim: A transaction committed in WAL mode with synchronous=NORMAL may roll back after a power loss or system crash.
quote: A transaction committed in WAL mode with synchronous=NORMAL might roll back following a power loss or system crash. always

claim: For transactions larger than about 100 MB, rollback journal modes will likely be faster than WAL, per the official docs.
quote: For transactions larger than about 100 megabytes, traditional rollback journal modes will likely be faster. always

claim: In wal2 mode the checkpointer must wait until writers have switched to the other WAL file before checkpointing.
quote: In wal2 mode, the checkpointer has to wait until writers have switched to the "other" wal file before a checkpoint can take place. always

claim: In rollback-journal mode, synchronous=FULL is not necessarily durable across a power loss.
quote: FULL is necessarily durable across a power loss in rollback mode.

claim: Setting EXCLUSIVE locking mode before the first WAL access avoids shared-memory use entirely, so no wal-index shm is created.
quote: If EXCLUSIVE locking mode is set prior to the first WAL-mode database access, then SQLite never attempts to call any of the shared-memory methods always

claim: With synchronous=NORMAL in WAL mode, the WAL is synced before each checkpoint and the database file is synced after each completed checkpoint.
quote: the WAL file is synchronized before each checkpoint and the database file is synchronized after each completed checkpoint, always

claim: For transactions larger than about 100 MB, rollback journal modes will likely be faster than WAL.
quote: For transactions larger than about 100 megabytes, traditional rollback journal modes will likely be faster. always

claim: With always-overlapping readers, checkpoints never complete and the WAL file grows without bound.
quote: then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound. always

claim: Opening a WAL database requires write privilege on the -shm file if it exists, or write access to the database directory if it does not.
quote: The opening process must have write privileges for "-shm" wal-index shared memory file associated with the database, if that file exists

claim: BEGIN IMMEDIATE starts a write transaction immediately and may fail with SQLITE_BUSY if another writer is active.
quote: The BEGIN IMMEDIATE might fail with SQLITE_BUSY if another write transaction is already active on another database connection.

claim: The WAL-index shared memory is created by mmapping a file in the same directory as the database, which is the only way SQLite found to ensure processes share it.
quote: create the shared memory by mmapping a file in the same directory as the database itself.

claim: WAL write transactions write content once, whereas rollback-journal transactions write it twice.
quote: Write transactions are very fast since they only involve writing the content once (versus twice for rollback-journal transactions)

claim: All automatic checkpoints run in PASSIVE mode.
quote: All automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE.

claim: In WAL mode, a transaction spanning multiple ATTACHed databases is atomic per database but not atomic across the set.
quote: Transactions that involve changes against multiple ATTACHed databases are atomic for each individual database, but are not atomic across all databases as a set.

claim: If another connection holds a read transaction open, the checkpoint cannot reset the WAL file.
quote: If another connection has a read transaction open, then the checkpoint cannot reset the WAL file

claim: In rollback-journal mode, any number of connections can hold SHARED locks at once, allowing many simultaneous readers.
quote: Any number of processes can hold SHARED locks at the same time, hence there can be many simultaneous readers.

claim: WAL mode is significantly faster than rollback journal in most scenarios.
quote: WAL is significantly faster in most scenarios.

claim: Since SQLite 3.11.0, WAL mode handles large transactions as efficiently as rollback mode.
quote: Beginning with version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15), WAL mode works as efficiently with large transactions as does rollback mode.

claim: WAL mode allows multiple simultaneous writers.
quote: WAL mode allows any number of concurrent writers to commit at the same time.

claim: synchronous=OFF is safe on power loss.
quote: With synchronous OFF the database cannot be corrupted by a power failure.

claim: Checkpoints never block readers.
quote: Checkpoints of every kind are guaranteed never to block a reader.

claim: WAL works on NFS.
quote: WAL mode is fully supported on network filesystems such as NFS.

claim: Default autocheckpoint is 10000 pages.
quote: By default SQLite checkpoints when the WAL reaches 10000 pages.
